fields.features_heading: Inside a Drag and Drop Quiz on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Each question is a set of cards and the slots they go in. Emergent builds both, plus the scoring and a table of every placement.
fields.feature_1:
Four drag types from one prompt

Describe the question in plain words, such as five fractions to order. Emergent builds the cards, the drop zones, and the answer key, and a follow-up prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Points for each card in its slot

Set the scoring rule: 1 point for every card in the right place, or nothing until all of them are. The app applies it when a taker submits, and the score shows on the next screen.
fields.feature_3:
A tap option beside every drag

Ask for a tap option, and Emergent builds it next to the drag: tap a card, then tap its slot. A taker who cannot drag on a small phone screen still finishes the same question.
fields.feature_4:
Every placement saved to your database

Each submission saves which card landed in which slot, in a database you own. Sort the rows by card, and the one placed wrong most often sits at the top, ready for the next lesson.
fields.feature_5:
Score emails and Slack alerts

The app emails each score to the taker and sends a Slack alert to the teacher when someone falls below the pass mark. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so a whole grade can play.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

Host the quiz on a custom domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep the quiz after the term ends.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Drag and Drop Quizzes at Work
fields.tab_content_1:
When 6 students put 1/3 before 1/4

Marisol Echeverry teaches fourth grade at Abernook Elementary. Her 26 students drag 5 fraction cards into order, smallest to largest, and the app gives 1 point per card in the right slot. All 5 landed in place for 18 of the 26. Six put 1/3 before 1/4, and Monday's warm-up compares those two.
fields.tab_content_2:
Under 10 of 12, every new hire sorts again

New hires at Varnhold Supply sort 12 item cards into the 3 bins on the company's waste chart before their first shift. A score of 10 or more passes. Anything lower sends the hire back to the training video and posts a Slack alert to the shift supervisor. In October, 11 of 14 new hires passed on the first try.
fields.tab_content_3:
The word for spoon, paired with a fork 9 times

Every Tuesday, 22 adult learners at Lintwhistle Language Center match 8 Spanish words to 8 pictures. The app saves each wrong pairing as its own row. This week, 9 of 22 dropped the word for spoon on the picture of a fork. Thursday's class opens with kitchen words.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any shopper who ranks chocolate first gets dark roast

Shoppers on the Graymoss Roasters site drag 5 flavor notes into the order they like them. The note ranked first picks one of 3 roasts for the result screen, and chocolate points to the dark roast. In October, 171 of 412 shoppers put chocolate first. The roaster's database keeps each ranking with the shopper's email address.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Drag and Drop Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan drag and drop quiz maker questions that score fairly and show what to reteach, then build them with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Add a decoy card or two
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the drag type before you write a card. Ordering tests sequence, sorting tests categories, matching tests pairs, and ranking collects preferences with no right answer. Put the type and the audience in your prompt, and Emergent builds the question around them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Keep every card label to a few words, such as a fraction or a single item name. A long sentence on a card is hard to read while a finger covers half of it. Put the longer explanation in the feedback a taker sees after submitting.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add one or two decoy cards that belong in no slot when the question is a sort or a match. Without a decoy, the last card always goes in the last open slot, and the taker gets a point for it without knowing the answer.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose between a point per card and all-or-nothing scoring before launch. A point per card shows how close a taker came on a 5-card order. All-or-nothing suits a safety step, where one card in the wrong place should count as a fail.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Offer a tap alternative to dragging
fields.howto_step_5_des: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.5.7, Level AA, asks that anything done with a dragging movement can also be done by a single pointer without dragging, unless dragging is essential. Ask for a tap-a-card, tap-a-slot option, and try the quiz with a keyboard as well.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Take the quiz on a phone held in one hand before anyone else does. Drag every card into a wrong slot at least once, then open the results table and confirm each placement scored the way you meant it to.
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the first round, look at the wrong placements for a pattern, such as one pair swapped by a quarter of the class. Decide whether to reteach the idea or rewrite the card, then change the question by prompt before the next round.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a drag and drop quiz maker for my fourth-grade math class that scores each fraction card a student places.

faq_plan.q: What is drag and drop quiz maker?
faq_plan.a: A drag and drop quiz maker is a tool for building quiz questions that takers answer by moving cards: putting steps in order, sorting items into groups, matching pairs, or labeling a picture. The tool checks where each card lands and scores the answer.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up drag and drop quiz maker?
faq_plan.a: Describe the quiz in Emergent's AI survey builder: who takes it, the cards, where each one belongs, and how it scores. Emergent builds the questions, the scoring, and the results database. Play it once yourself, change anything by prompt, then share the link.

faq_plan.q: Can a drag and drop quiz maker give partial credit?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when you set the scoring that way. With a point per card, a taker who places 4 of 5 cards correctly scores 4. All-or-nothing scoring gives the same answer 0. Pick one rule per question, and say which it is in the instructions so nobody is surprised by a score.

faq_plan.q: Can I use a drag and drop quiz maker for free?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing. Describe the cards and the slots, play the quiz once yourself, and share the link with your first group of takers.

faq_plan.q: Does a drag and drop quiz maker work on phones and tablets?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when each question responds to touch and every card is big enough for a fingertip. Ask for touch dragging and a tap-to-place option in your prompt. Then test on a real phone, because a mouse on a laptop hides the problems a thumb finds.

faq_plan.q: Can a drag and drop quiz maker support keyboard users?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when every card can move without a mouse: Tab to reach a card, Enter or Space to pick it up, the arrow keys to move it, and Enter to drop it. Describe that pattern in your prompt, then run the whole quiz once without touching the mouse.

faq_plan.q: How many cards per question should I use in a drag and drop quiz maker?
faq_plan.a: As many as fit on one phone screen with no scrolling. A taker who has to scroll while holding a card drops it in the wrong place. Test on the smallest phone your takers use, and split the question in two if the slots run off the screen.

faq_plan.q: What question types can a drag and drop quiz maker build?
faq_plan.a: You can build ordering, sorting, matching, and labeling questions, plus ranking for preferences with no right answer, such as a product finder. One quiz can mix several kinds. Emergent builds each question from your description, and adding a new kind takes one more sentence in the prompt.

faq_plan.q: How do I add an answer key in a drag and drop quiz maker?
faq_plan.a: Write the answer key into your prompt: each card and the slot it belongs in, or the correct order for a sequence. The app checks every placement against that key on submit. To show answers afterward, ask for a review screen that puts each wrong card next to its right slot.

faq_plan.q: Can a drag and drop quiz maker show which cards each student got wrong?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Every attempt is stored per student. Open one student's quiz to see each card that missed its slot, or filter a whole class by a single card. The records sit in a database you own, and they stay there after the term ends.
